## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- explain why a producer should not enumerate its consumers
- add a subscription without changing producer code
- distinguish event-contract stability from consumer implementation
- extend the Angular workflow through a stable host context

## Producer knowledge creates coupling

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Producer[Rental producer] --> Published[(Stable published List)]
    Published --> Router[Event router]
    Router --> Rental[Rental consumer]
    Router --> Insurance[Insurance consumer]
    Router --> Future[Future consumer]
```

The producer publishes one business fact. Subscription descriptors tell the
router which consumer queues receive a copy.

## Subscription descriptors

```json
{
  "consumer": "insurance-service",
  "eventType": "AuctionWon",
  "eventVersion": 1,
  "queue": "auction:events:simple:insurance-service:ready"
}
```

A new consumer adds configuration and its own queue. The producer contract and
deployment can remain unchanged.

## Router delivery and duplicates

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant I as Published List
    participant R as Routing List
    participant D as Router
    participant C as Consumer Lists
    D->>I: LMOVE published to routing
    D->>C: RPUSH one copy per subscription
    D->>R: LREM acknowledgement
```

A crash during fan-out can deliver to some queues before retry. Every consumer
therefore retains its own idempotence boundary.

## Event evolution

Changing the meaning of an existing field forces independent consumers to
coordinate. Prefer a new version or event type when meaning changes.

During migration:

- keep V1 readable
- publish or translate V2 explicitly
- test examples for each supported version
- retire V1 only after consumer evidence confirms migration

## Angular extension boundary

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Host[Rental validation page] --> Registry[Generated extension registry]
    Registry --> Insurance[Insurance panel]
    Context[Stable rental context] --> Insurance
    Registry --> Future[Future extension]
    Context --> Future
```

Each extension owns its component, API client, models, and descriptor. The host
supplies rental context without importing insurance-specific types.

## End-to-end feature ownership

A new optional service may require:

- an event subscription and idempotent backend consumer
- owned persistence and API endpoints
- one Angular extension and descriptor
- deployment, health, tests, and operating evidence

The shared contracts remain deliberately small.

## Module investigation

1. Add a notification subscription descriptor on paper.
2. Trace how the Angular registry is generated.
3. List files owned by the Insurance extension.
4. Identify a router crash point that can create duplicates.
